Transfluidized lung injury is a type of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) that occurs after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), which is a life support therapy for patients with severe respiratory failure or cardiac arrest. It is characterized by alveolar flooding, pulmonary edema, hypoxemia, and inflammation. The most common cause of transfluidizing lung injury after ECMO is the removal of large volumes of plasma from the blood stream, which can reduce the intravascular volume and alter the osmotic pressure, leading to fluid shift into the interstitial space and alveoli. Other factors that can contribute to transfluidity are hemolysis, infection, coagulopathy, and metabolic acidosis.

B. B

D. D
subject: Psychiatry

An individual who has Histrionic Personality Disorder (HPD) is a person who is overly dramatic, attention-seeking, and tends to be very emotional in social settings. They often exaggerate their emotions or behaviors to gain attention from others. People with this disorder may also have difficulty maintaining close relationships due to their need for constant validation and approval. Individuals with Shyness Personality Disorder are typically introverted and prefer solitude or small groups of people they know well. They tend to feel uncomfortable in new situations or around unfamiliar people. Those with Anxiety Avoidant Personality Disorder have an intense fear of rejection, criticism, and disapproval from others, leading them to avoid social interactions altogether. Individuals who fall into Cluster A – Paranoid, Schizoid, and Schizotypal personality disorders, tend to display eccentric behavior and have difficulty forming close relationships with others.

Explanation:
Anorexia Nervosa (AN) is a serious eating disorder characterized by a refusal to maintain body weight at or above normal range and fear of gaining weight even when underweight. The mainstay of treatment for AN is nutritional rehabilitation and weight restoration through gradual increase in daily caloric intake. In this case, despite following the prescribed diet plan, the patient has not gained any weight. Increasing the daily caloric consumption from 1500 to 2000 calories can help the patient achieve the desired weight gain. This will also ensure that the patient receives enough nutrients to support their overall health and well-being.

instruction:
Which of the following is activated by intrinsic or extrinsic pathway's?
A. Necroptosis
B. Apoptosis
C. Necrosis
D. Pyroptosis
subject: Pathology
full_response:
The correct option is B. Apoptois
Explanation:
Apoptosis is a programmed cell death that occurs in multicellular organisms to remove unnecessary, damaged, or infected cells. It can be triggered by both intrinsic (intrusion of apoptotic signal molecules into the cell) and extrinsical (interaction of apoptosis-inducing ligands on the cell surface receptors).
Necrosis is an uncontrolled cell death due to injury or stress. It is not a regulated process and leads to inflammation and tissue damage.
Necroptosis is also known as pyroptotic cell death. It involves the activation of caspases and release of inflammatory cytokines. It differs from apoptosis in terms of the cellular membrane permeabilization and mitochondrial dysfunction.
Pyroptoses are rare forms of necrotic cell death caused by bacterial toxins or viruses. Examples include diphtheria toxin-induced necrosis and herpes simplex virus-induced necroptotic death.

instruction:
Which of the following is the complication of massive blood transfusion?
A. Metabolic acidosis
B. Metabolic alkalosis
C. Respiratory alkalosis
D. Respiratory acidosis
subject: Pathology
full_response:
The correct option is B. Metabolism alkalotic reaction.
Explanation:
Massive blood transfusions usually lead to metabolic alkaloses due to dilution of the plasma sodium level, which leads to an increase in extracellular fluid volume (ECF) and a decrease in intracellular fluid (ICF). This causes water to shift out of cells into ECF, leading to cellular dehydration and the release of protons from the cytoplasmic compartment, resulting in respiratory alkalization.

instruction:
Which of the following diseases is diagnosed with the help of the flowcytometry pattern?
A. Bruton disease
B. Bare lymphocyte syndrome
C. Hyper IgM syndrome

subject: Pathology
full_response:
The correct option is D. Sevee Combined Immunodeficiencies Disease.
Explanation:
Severe combined immune deficiency (SCID) disease is a group of inherited disorders that cause an absence of or dysfunction of certain types of white blood cells, which are essential to protect us from infections and other diseases. SCID can be caused by mutations in genes involved in immune cell development, function, or survival. The most common type of SCID is X-linked severe combined immuno deficiency (XSCID), which affects boys more than girls because it is carried on the X chromosome. Boys only need one copy of the mutated gene to develop the disease, while girls need two copies. 
The main symptom of SCIDs is recurrent and severe bacterial or viral infections, which can lead to serious complications such as pneumonia, meningitis, sepsis, or organ failure. Some patients may also have other symptoms such as skin rash, diarrhea, enlarged spleen, thymus gland, or bone marrow.

instruction:
Which of the following finding are there in iron deficiency anemia?
A. | TIBC, | Ferritin, | Transferrin saturation
B. | TIBC, | Ferritin, | Transferrin saturation
C. | TIBC, | Ferritin, | Transferrin saturation
D. | TIBC, | Ferritin, | Transferrin saturation
subject: Pathology
full_response:
A | TIBI, | FERRI, | TRANSFERRIN SATURATION

Explanation:
Iron deficiency anemias can have a variety of signs and symptoms. One of these is low levels of transferrin (TIBI) and ferritin (FERRI), which are proteins that transport and store iron respectively. A decrease in both of these levels indicates that the body has insufficient iron stores to meet its needs. Another sign of iron deficiency is high levels of serum transferrin saturation (TRANSFERRIND SATURATON). This occurs when there is not enough iron available to bind to transferrin, so the remaining iron becomes saturated with it. Therefore, the correct answer is B, as all three findings are related to iron deficiency.
